review.raw_markdown: ### 1. Executive Summary A functional but underperforming cart abandonment email. The hook is clever, the product is visible, and there's a clear CTA — but the email immediately dilutes the abandonment urgency by piling on recommendation modules, a BOGO offer, a category nav menu, and app-download prompts. The hero does its job; everything below it works against conversion focus. --- ### 2. Business Impact Score: 5 / 10 Gets the basics right but squanders the abandonment moment with too many competing objectives. --- ### 3. What's Working - **Headline voice.** "We noticed you noticing us..." is playful and self-aware — it earns attention without being pushy or fear-of-missing-out heavy. - **Product hero is present.** The abandoned shoe is shown clearly with its name and a single, direct CTA button ("Complete Your Order"). No ambiguity about what the email is for. - **BOGO offer is prominent.** A "Buy One, Get One 50% Off" banner is visually distinct and adds genuine purchase incentive. - **Payment flexibility is surfaced.** Afterpay and Klarna logos appear, which addresses a real friction point (price hesitation) at the right moment. --- ### 4. What's Weak - **Urgency is absent.** Nothing in the email conveys that the cart has a shelf life. No countdown, no low-stock signal, no "expires in X hours." This is the single biggest miss for a cart abandonment flow. - **Recommendation module undermines the job.** The "Here's Some More Great Options We Think You'll Love" section with a Shop All Best Sellers CTA pulls the reader away from completing the original transaction. It's a competing goal inserted at exactly the wrong moment. - **Category navigation is noise.** A full Women's / Men / Kids / Clothing / New Arrivals / Sale link list belongs in a newsletter, not a cart recovery email. It offers too many exits. - **The BOGO offer is unanchored.** It's not clear if the 50% off applies to the abandoned item or requires an additional purchase. The ambiguity could cause hesitation rather than resolve it. - **"Let's Get Texting" / app download block is off-mission.** Recruiting SMS subscribers and app installs mid-cart-recovery is a channel acquisition ask that competes with the purchase conversion goal. - **The email is long.** By the time the reader gets to payment options and store finder, they've already been given five other things to do. Scroll depth will kill conversion rate on the lower modules. --- ### 5. Recommendations 1. **Add urgency above the CTA.** A single line — "Your cart expires in 24 hours" or "Only X pairs left" — does more work than anything else on this list. 2. **Cut or move the recommendation module.** If cross-sell is a must, move it below the fold or trigger it in a separate follow-up email 24 hours later. 3. **Clarify the BOGO offer scope.** One sentence: "Buy your Maxroad + any second pair and get 50% off." Remove the guesswork. 4. **Remove the category nav and app download block** from this send entirely. Reserve them for browse abandonment or newsletter sends. 5. **Tighten the layout to three sections:** Hero + CTA → Urgency/incentive (BOGO) → Payment flexibility. Everything else is distraction at this funnel stage. --- ### 6. Bottom Line Skechers has the raw ingredients for a solid cart abandonment email but has structured it like a general promotional send. The playful tone and visible product are assets worth keeping. Strip the email to its core job — get the shoe in the cart across the finish line — and this becomes a meaningfully better performer. --- ### 7. Evidence **Overall purpose:** Cart abandonment recovery. The subject line and hero headline make the intent explicit. **Hero / primary value proposition:** Abandoned shoe (Maxroad, based on visible product image) shown with name, image, and one CTA button. Clean and functional, though the CTA button styling is understated — it doesn't visually dominate the fold. **Membership / benefits section:** None visible. No loyalty program callout, no member-exclusive messaging. **Product discoverability / recommendation modules:** One "best options" recommendation row with approximately 3 product tiles and a "Shop All Best Sellers" CTA. Visually present but strategically misplaced in this flow. **Utility / secondary modules:** Category navigation accordion (Women's, Men, Kids, Clothing, New Arrivals, Sale), app download (App Store + Google Play), Shop Now Pay Later (Afterpay + Klarna), Find a Store link, social follow icons (Facebook, Instagram). All present and rendered cleanly. **Bugs / friction / clarity issues:** No broken images or rendering failures visible. The email renders cleanly. The product images in the recommendation row are small and low-contrast against the white background, making individual styles difficult to distinguish at a glance. --- ## Technical Audit ## Technical Audit — SKECHERS "Your Items Are Waiting!" (Abandoned Cart) --- ### 1. Technical Summary The email is built on a standard table-based layout via Attentive ESP and renders correctly at a structural level. Primary technical concerns are HTTP-only link/image URLs, an empty `` element, and no confirmable UTM parameters in the click-redirect chain from the truncated source. --- ### 2. Link & Tracking Issues **HTTP redirect domain (confirmed):** All CTA links and the "web version" link route through `http://skechers.attentivemail.com/ls/click?upn=…` — plaintext HTTP, not HTTPS. Example: ``` http://skechers.attentivemail.com/ls/click?upn=u001.LNc6VorXOZu5avyAvDTfGTW… ``` Gmail, Outlook, and Apple Mail mark outbound HTTP redirects as potentially insecure; some corporate proxies will block or warn on them. **HTTP image host (confirmed):** The logo `<img src="http://image.emails.skechers.…` loads over HTTP. Clients that enforce HTTPS (e.g., Outlook 365 with strict proxy configs) may block or badge-warn these images. **UTM attribution — not confirmable from source:** No `utm_source`, `utm_medium`, `utm_campaign`, or `utm_content` parameters appear in the raw `href` values before the Attentive redirect fires. If the redirect does not inject UTMs on the way through, GA4 / site analytics will classify all cart-recovery traffic as `(direct) / (none)`. --- ### 3. Rendering & Accessibility **Empty `<title>` tag:** ```html <title> ``` Accessibility tools and some screen readers surface the `` as the document label in tab/window context. It should be set to the subject line or a descriptive equivalent. **Preheader padding technique — functional but brittle:** The preheader uses a mix of U+034F (Combining Grapheme Joiner `͏`) and U+00AD (Soft Hyphen `­`) characters to pad white space. This is common practice but some aggressive spam filters flag high Unicode-character-density in hidden content. The two character classes have different rendering behavior across clients; a single consistent padding character (e.g., `‌`) is more reliable. **`lang="en"` on `<html>` — correct.** **`charset=utf-8` meta and `viewport` meta present — correct.** **`#MessageViewBody a` Gmail link color override present — correct.** **Image `alt` text — not confirmable:** The `<img>` tag for the logo is cut off in the truncated source before the `alt` attribute appears. If `alt` is absent or empty on a linked image, screen readers will read the URL string; if `alt` is present but blank, the link has no accessible label. Verify `alt` is set to descriptive text (e.g., `"Skechers"`) on all linked images. --- ### 4. Personalization & Merge Tokens No merge tokens (e.g., `{{first_name}}`, `{{cart_items}}`, `{{cart_total}}`, `{{product_image_url}}`) are visible in the source fragment provided. For an abandoned cart trigger: - The subject line `"Your Items Are Waiting!"` contains no first-name token. - No cart item block with dynamic product name, image, price, or quantity is visible in the truncated source. This may indicate that dynamic product rendering occurs in a lower section of the HTML not included here, or that the send used static fallback content. The full source should be checked to confirm cart-item merge tags are present and not rendering as raw token strings. --- ### 5. Compliance (CAN-SPAM, Unsubscribe, Authentication) **Unsubscribe link and physical mailing address** — not visible in the truncated source. CAN-SPAM §5 requires a functioning opt-out mechanism and a valid physical postal address in every commercial email. Confirm both are present in the full HTML footer. **Authentication headers** — not derivable from HTML source alone. For `msgs.skechers.com` (sending subdomain), SPF, DKIM, and DMARC alignment should be verified via raw message headers. The sending domain structure (`msgs.skechers.com`) is consistent with ESP subdomain delegation, which is standard, but authentication pass/fail cannot be assessed from HTML. **Preheader disclosure** — the hidden preheader text (`"You left something in your cart, get it before it's gone! Join Skechers Plus today for free shipping!"`) accurately reflects email content. No deceptive header language detected. --- ### 6. Email-to-Site Continuity **UTM gap (high risk):** As noted in §2, no UTM parameters are embedded in the `href` values pre-redirect. If Attentive's redirect layer appends UTMs, verify that: - `utm_medium=email` (not `email_click` or similar non-standard value) - `utm_source=attentive` or `skechers_email` - `utm_campaign` includes a consistent campaign slug (e.g., `abandoned_cart`) - `utm_content` differentiates individual CTAs (logo vs. product block vs. CTA button) Without content-level UTM differentiation, click-source breakdowns within the campaign are unattributable. **Landing page destination** — the redirect target URLs are opaque (Attentive-encoded). Spot-decode at least the primary CTA URL to confirm it lands on the correct cart recovery or product page, not the homepage. --- ### 7. Recommendations | Priority | Issue | Action | |---|---|---| | High | HTTP redirect and image URLs | Migrate `attentivemail.com` click-tracking and `image.emails.skechers.com` to HTTPS. Coordinate with Attentive account settings. | | High | UTM parameter coverage | Confirm Attentive injects UTMs on redirect; if not, encode them in the pre-redirect `href`. Add `utm_content` per CTA. | | Medium | Empty `<title>` tag | Set to subject line or `"Skechers — Abandoned Cart Reminder"`. | | Medium | Cart item merge token audit | Decode full HTML and verify dynamic product blocks render with real tokens before send. | | Medium | Unsubscribe / physical address | Confirm CAN-SPAM footer is present in full source. | | Low | Preheader padding character consistency | Replace mixed U+034F/U+00AD padding with uniform `‌` sequences. | | Low | Image `alt` text | Verify all linked `<img>` elements carry descriptive `alt` values. |
